claims.text: At stage-3 DonHang.Catalog exports exactly CatalogModule (registers Catalog's services at startup), CatalogProduct (copy of a product's values that ICatalog returns) and ICatalog; Product (a row of products) is internal. ICatalog has no rename method. Catalog.csproj has no ProjectReference.

claims.text: The compiler rejects code in another assembly that names an internal type. Changing a type from internal to public compiles, and so does a new ProjectReference from DonHang.Catalog to DonHang.Domain, which references no Catalog project.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: Access modifiers (internal); compiler error CS0122; MSBuild ProjectReference item

claims.text: CatalogUsesNoOrderingProject reads the Catalog assembly's referenced assemblies, keeps names in ProjectsCatalogMustNotUse (Domain, Infrastructure, Api) and calls Assert.Empty. DonHang.Api.csproj references DonHang.Catalog. The class has 5 test cases; 3 guard Notifications, Payments, Messaging.
A compiled assembly records a reference to another assembly only when its code uses a type from it; a ProjectReference with no code using it leaves no entry in GetReferencedAssemblies.
claims.source_hint: Assembly.GetReferencedAssemblies API docs; same claim verified in design.l2.testing-the-dependency-rule (Try it step 1)

claims.text: CatalogMakesPublicOnlyItsContract takes GetExportedTypes() of the Catalog assembly, selects Type.Name, sorts with Order() and calls Assert.Equal(CatalogPublicTypes, exported) where CatalogPublicTypes = [CatalogModule, CatalogProduct, ICatalog].
Assembly.GetExportedTypes returns the public types defined in the assembly that are visible outside it; internal types are not included.
claims.source_hint: Assembly.GetExportedTypes API docs (Remarks: only public types visible outside the assembly)

claims.text: xUnit Assert.Equal on two string sequences compares them item by item in order and fails on any extra, missing or different item, with the message 'Assert.Equal() Failure: Collections differ' and Expected/Actual lines.

claims.text: ModuleBoundaryTests needs no architecture-testing package: DonHang.Tests.csproj references only Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk, xunit, xunit.runner.visualstudio, Testcontainers and Mvc.Testing packages.

Keeping the allowed list in the test makes widening a contract a visible edit in the pull request; this pays when the contract is small and rarely changes, and becomes noise if public types change in most pull requests, where checking references alone may serve better.
claims.source_hint: design judgement; outline items 3-4; misconception 2; ModuleBoundaryTests.cs:23-25 comment

claims.text: A dedicated architecture-testing library can be worth adopting when the rules grow beyond what a few assertions express; two plain [Fact] methods suffice for Catalog's boundary.
These tests check structure only (references and public types); they cannot tell whether a call made through ICatalog, such as ChangePriceAsync, is sensible.
